scope: Independent inspection of GRUB-to-Linux diagnostic boot; not userspace or GPU qualification
observed: GRUB executes the unmodified kernel with explicit boot arguments including noapic and nokaslr.
Linux serial reaches HPET clocksource registration.
Terminal stack is inside IRQ handling; this alone does not establish an interrupt storm.
remaining: Reach userspace with standard interrupt routing.
Diagnose timer/IRQ progress and boot throughput.
Run actual GLX workload before enabling PC GPU admission.

symbolization.method: Unique match of all16 recorded instruction bytes in exact kernel ELF PT_LOAD segments.

post_elcr.scope: ELCR/PIC correction has not established full boot. Terminal timing code alone does not prove a timer stall or interrupt storm.

post_elcr_trace.symbolization_method: 36 uniquely matching instruction-byte sequences among the first40 trace entries agree on the slide in the exact kernel ELF PT_LOAD segments; llvm-addr2line resolves the complete trace with that slide.
observed_transitions: timer_interrupt returns through common_interrupt and native_irq_return_iret
handle_softirqs is followed by a new irq_entries_start/common_interrupt entry
second timer_interrupt reaches tick_periodic and timekeeping_advance
post_elcr_trace.conclusion: The bounded trace observes repeated timer IRQ servicing, rather than a single stuck fast_mix instruction. Controller state and timer-rate evidence are still needed to diagnose why Linux has not reached userspace.
